correctness.rationale: For each integer m!=0 the three factor vectors u=(1,4m), v=(2,2m), w=(4,m) satisfy 2u-5v+2w=0, producing an exact odd closed walk of length nine. Avoiding all three vectors gives at most four E-vertices among nine cyclic positions. Uniform square-boundary estimates prove d*(E)<=4/9. E0 has density 4/9 and excludes all six complete product-four difference vectors; E1 excludes all 2 mod4 coordinate products, proving K>=4 for delta<=1/2. The over-1/2 intersection argument gives P(E)=Z. Finite verifier tests exactly the critical local relations, not the infinite-domain proof.

value.rationale: The 2026 same-set positive-density theorem proves existence of a modulus K(delta) but gives no explicit optimal high-density portion. Determining its exact constant 4 on the entire interval (4/9,1/2], together with a sharp density boundary and explicit extremizers, is a natural quantitative refinement. The nine-cycle exhibits a genuine correlation obstruction that does not follow from one-dimensional product theorems or the routine d*>1/2 pigeonhole argument.
